name: refuse-deprovisioned-endpoint
description: A deprovisioned app answers EVERY JSON-RPC request on its per-app MCP endpoint (initialize included) with HTTP 403 and a JSON-RPC error whose data.refusal carries the registry projection — code, message, fix, retry, appId — so the client reads app_deprovisioned instead of guessing between a deleted app and a bad credential. error.code is -32003 (APP_NOT_FOUND — the endpoint no longer serves this app) and error.message is App not found; an untyped authorization failure answers -32007 (UNAUTHORIZED) with no data, so a client can tell the two apart by code and can tell neither from a dropped socket by mistake — -32000 is the SDK client's ConnectionClosed and a first-party server never chooses it (ggui#836).

refusal.message: the app record has no owner claim any more — the app was deprovisioned
refusal.fix: provision the app again; this app id never renders again
